description:
I spent 13 years building Android apps, and for most of them, the backend was someone else’s problem. Building Weather Pal, my own forecast app, broke that habit fast. It taught me that mobile reliability is rarely about whether your server responded. It is about what happens to your data between fetch and display, and about who else is drinking from the pipe you pay for. Two incidents made that concrete. In the first, the operating system quietly stopped refreshing my data. In the second, scripts I had never authorised drained the quota that would have refreshed it. Neither showed up as an error.

title: What building an Android weather app taught me about designing for reliability
